A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RE-ALIGN and rDPO. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination and VQA evaluations, model-scaling experiments, objective comparisons, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, ablations, and a semantic-similarity analysis.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 is identical and moves to Appendix A. Retrieval, segment masking, preference generation, and the default DPO-plus-vDPO objective remain unchanged. Sentence masking and alternative loss weights are tested as ablation variants.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the LLaVA-Instruct-150K training source and the same hallucination and general-VQA benchmarks. New analyses reuse existing coverage; narrowing the objective ablation does not remove those benchmarks from the paper.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add LLaVA-RLHF and mDPO for LLaVA-v1.5-7B. Table 3 adds those comparators and HSA-DPO for LLaVA-v1.5-13B. This substantially broadens comparison methods, including mDPO, which v1 discussed without evaluating. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: New protocols test similarity thresholds 0.85/0.90/0.95, sentence versus segment masking, five visual-loss weights from 0 to 1, and caption-to-image CLIP similarities for original/retrieved/random images. Section 4.3 narrows its benchmark subset to ScienceQA, TextVQA, and POPE. The main 11k-image, one-epoch, temperature-zero settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds threshold and masking ablations, replaces the broad DPO/rDPO comparison with a narrower loss-weight sweep, and analyzes retrieved-image semantic relevance. These substantially expand investigation of data curation and visual supervision. The dataset-size study and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new semantic-similarity averages do not introduce uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores persist, but numerous comparator and ablation results are added, including CLIP means of 0.2780/0.2382/0.0688. Table 2's vanilla LLaVA-v1.5-7B average rank changes from 3.375 to 3.875 with expanded comparators. Some v1 Table 4 DPO results, including Mistral results and additional LLaVA-v1.5 metrics, are no longer reported.

T1.justification: The existing mathematical definitions and core objectives are retained, with no added proofs, derivations, or formal guarantees. The weighted-loss expression parameterizes an empirical ablation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: retrieval-based dual preferences, rDPO, hallucination mitigation, general-VQA improvements, and scalability across model sizes and architectures.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of threshold and loss-weight trade-offs and explains retrieved images as plausible rejected inputs in Section 5. Appendix F expands the alignment-tax explanation to reduced retention of pretraining knowledge. Existing performance limitations and societal-risk discussion remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies top-10 retrieval and documents the caption prompt for its semantic-similarity analysis. It removes v1's code-release statement and repository pointer. Existing masking prompts, LoRA settings, hyperparameters, hardware, costs, and training times remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including Sun et al. (2023), Xiao et al. (2025), Xie et al. (2024), and Fu et al. (2024), alongside additional application references. Appendix B expands baseline descriptions. The central novelty positioning and related-work narrative remain stable.

P1.justification: Section 4.3 becomes 'Ablation Study'; Algorithm 1 and the segment-level/data-size discussion move into appendices. There are localized prose corrections and an added author, Chan-wei Hu. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 gain comparator rows, and v1's wide Table 4 is replaced by three compact ablation tables. The dataset-size plot moves to the appendix, with figure renumbering and page reflow. Existing figure graphics and qualitative illustrations are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added mDPO comparison and direct threshold/masking tests strengthen support for important design choices that v1 mostly justified verbally. The gain is limited: v2 omits broader DPO-only results and the code pointer, and Table 6 repeats intermediate-weight scores while its prose still claims two backbones without corresponding labeled results.
